claims: C1: In an interactive setting, when the assistant is given a transformation task, it may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted.
C2: The alert is a permissible, non-required behavior — the clause says 'may want to', not 'should' or 'must'.

concepts.name: transformation_interactive_alert
concepts.gloss: A is an alert to the user that changes to the text are warranted, given a transformation task in an interactive setting

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document

concepts.name: interactive_vs_programmatic_setting
concepts.gloss: S is an interactive setting where the assistant is interacting with a human in real time, as opposed to a programmatic setting where output is consumed programmatically

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule carrying user-level instruction authority, as in the #avoid_overstepping section

concepts.name: transformation_task
concepts.gloss: T is a task asking the assistant to transform text, such as translating between languages, adding annotations, or changing formatting

concepts.name: changes_warranted
concepts.gloss: C is a change to the text that the user or developer asked to be changed, so alerting about it is warranted
concepts.inference: The clause says 'changes to the text are warranted' — this presupposes a notion of which changes are warranted, which the surrounding text ties to what the user or developer asked to be changed.

ontology.gloss: A is an alert to the user that changes to the text are warranted, given a transformation task in an interactive setting

asserts.read_back: In an interactive setting, the assistant may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted

closure.reason: The clause says the assistant 'may want to' alert the user, which permits but does not require the alert; it does not forbid any alert, so silence permits.
